A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAOT research and contain readable main texts and appendices A–G. Text extraction, rendered pages, and matched graphics support reliable comparison across moves and renumbering; no essential material remains unavailable.

before.justification: V1 reports original GAOT benchmark results, DrivAerNet++ predictions, computational measurements, ablations, scaling experiments, and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: V3 retains original GAOT experiments and adds DrivAerML and NASA-CRM evaluations, component ablations, neural-field comparisons, and runtime analyses.

M1.justification: The core MAGNO–transformer architecture and training objectives remain. V3 makes targeted 3D adaptations: radius neighborhoods become merged radius/KNN graphs (B.5), and geometry embeddings are used only in the encoder rather than both encoder and decoder (F.4). These change the procedure beyond merely documenting existing settings.

E1.justification: V3 adds DrivAerML car aerodynamics with higher-fidelity simulations and approximately nine million surface points, plus NASA-CRM full-aircraft aerodynamics. Their pressure and shear/friction prediction tasks expand coverage beyond v1's DrivAerNet++ industrial evaluation; the earlier 2D coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The time-dependent comparison in Table 1 replaces RIGNO-12 with UPT, although both appear elsewhere in the paper. V3 also adds a ViT-only comparator to the regular-grid benchmarks (E.5) and explicit comparisons against classical numerical solvers (E.11), substantially broadening the comparison questions.

E3.justification: Table B.1 changes the stated DrivAerNet++ training budget from 200 to 50 epochs; this establishes a reported setting change, without proving which experiments were rerun. New protocols include quarter-resolution NACA0012 training followed by full-resolution testing, runtime profiling at batch sizes 1 and 32, and comparison with a coarsened numerical solver.

E4.justification: V3 adds ViT-only ablations testing encoder/decoder contributions, three geometry-embedding placements on industrial datasets, and a NACA0012 neural-field comparison with UPT. Component runtime profiling and solver coarsening further examine efficiency mechanisms and accuracy–cost tradeoffs. V1's tokenization, time-stepping, multiscale, scaling, and transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report six independent Bluff-Body training runs with mean error 2.39 ± 0.12% (v1 Table E.4; v3 Table E.8). The stated averaging of computational measurements over 100 repetitions also remains. No new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes GAOT's pressure MSE entry from 4.9409 to 4.2694 and wall-shear-stress MSE from 8.7370 to 8.6878, both in units of 10^-2; accompanying 3D method and training changes prevent treating these as controlled gains. V3 adds industrial, UPT, ViT, profiling, and ablation results. The new ViT comparison also changes rankings, beating GAOT on regular-grid NS-SL and NS-SVS.

T1.justification: V3 adds comparative asymptotic complexity expressions and memory-cost reasoning in E.1. It also corrects the Bernstein polynomial factor in Eq. D.8 from (1-xi)^i to (1-xi)^(n-i). The existing operator definitions remain, and neither version supplies GAOT approximation theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the industrial state-of-the-art claim from one dataset to three, including aerospace applications. Section 4 additionally claims a four-to-nine-order runtime advantage over classical PDE solvers. These extend the headline claims beyond v1's reported neural-baseline comparisons, irrespective of whether the stronger claims are fully supported.

C2.justification: V3 introduces a substantive qualification: decoder geometry embeddings can degrade industrial performance, attributed to overfitting and complex graph construction. It also interprets the ViT-only results to distinguish processor and encoder/decoder contributions, explains batching-related efficiency advantages, and identifies graph construction as a major DrivAerML inference bottleneck.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's mostly default configurations, v3 specifies industrial latent-grid dimensions, ten transformer layers, radius/KNN settings including k=1, and hardware and training details for the added datasets (B.5–B.6). Runtime sections expand implementation and resource disclosures. Source-code access instructions also change from a repository link to a project page.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for DrivAerML, the aerospace benchmark, Transolver++, AROMA, CVit, and Text2PDE, while removing two approximation/error-analysis references. The main positioning against message-passing, Fourier-based, and transformer-based operators remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence, appendices A–G, and most existing prose remain. V3 adds an appendix table of contents and targeted subsections, revises industrial-results and mechanism discussion, and updates author and conference information. The language and structural editing is localized despite the substantive additions.

P2.justification: V3 adds industrial visualizations in Figure 5 and Figures G.10–G.13, the graph-construction diagram B.3, and new benchmark, complexity, profiling, and ablation tables. Existing comparator columns and DrivAerNet++ renderings change, alongside conference formatting and redistributed floats. Most earlier PDE plots are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single industrial benchmark, v3 provides broader 3D evidence, informative component ablations, and clearer implementation details, improving validation and interpretability. These gains are partly offset by weaker claim calibration: the added industrial benchmarks compare only against GINO despite broader state-of-the-art wording, and Table E.9's speedup claims mix CPU core-hours with inference elapsed time and contain ratios inconsistent with the listed timings.
